title: "Can the borrower cover its interest?"
summary: "Trace a policy change through a floating-rate loan and distinguish a financing shock from a change in operating earnings."
base: ..
sectionname: Chapters
kicker: "Chapter 24 · Policy transmission"

::: {.decision}
**Your decision.** A company earns HK$6 million before interest and tax and owes HK$50 million on a floating-rate loan. Its lender requires interest coverage of at least 2.0 times. Could a rate rise cause a breach even before customers cut spending?
:::

## Read the contract before forecasting demand

Interest coverage equals annual earnings before interest and tax (EBIT) divided by annual interest. The loan pays a reference rate plus 2 percentage points and resets immediately for a full year. Its outstanding principal is constant. Initially the reference rate is 3%, so interest is 50 × 5% = **HK$2.5 million** and coverage is **2.40**.

| Scenario | Loan rate | EBIT, HK$ m | Interest, HK$ m | Coverage |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Before the change | 5% | 6.0 | 2.5 | 2.40 |
| Reference rate rises 2 percentage points | 7% | 6.0 | 3.5 | 1.71 |
| Customers also defer orders | 7% | 5.4 | 3.5 | 1.54 |
| Public procurement lifts EBIT to 7.2 | 7% | 7.2 | 3.5 | 2.06 |

The contractual reset alone breaks the threshold. At 7% the borrower needs EBIT of **HK$7 million** to restore coverage to 2.0. The last row is a separate scenario. For fiscal support to help this borrower, the company must win work, deliver it, and retain enough margin for EBIT to reach 7.2.

## Separate the channels and their timing

A monetary tightening can raise reference rates. Credit reprices on contractual reset dates. Higher financing costs can also lead customers to defer investment, shifting expenditure and output lower. The effect on inflation depends in part on spare capacity and the time prices take to adjust. Government purchases can increase demand directly. If productive capacity is tight, part of the response may appear in prices and costs. The scenario table gives conditional calculations for one borrower and leaves the size of the aggregate response open.

<details><summary>What if half the loan is fixed at 5%?</summary>
<p>With 25 fixed at 5% and 25 resetting to 7%, annual interest is 1.25 + 1.75 = HK$3 million. With unchanged EBIT of 6, coverage is exactly 2.0. If EBIT falls to 5.4 it declines to 1.8. For a credit memo, ask for the fixing schedule and the order book. They inform different parts of the ratio.</p>
</details>

<details><summary>Connect the calculation to the IS–MP model</summary>
<p>The IS relationship describes expenditure consistent with goods-market equilibrium at a given real rate. A tighter policy rule can raise the real rate at a given level of activity when inflation expectations are slow to adjust. Output then falls along the IS curve. A fiscal expansion shifts desired expenditure outward. A central bank response to inflation can offset part of the output gain. The loan contract passes a nominal reference rate into cash interest, so it also matters how inflation expectations evolve.</p>
</details>

```{=html}
<section class="panel" id="policy-transmission-lab" aria-labelledby="policy-transmission-lab-title">
<h2 id="policy-transmission-lab-title">Stress-test a loan covenant</h2><p>The borrower owes HK$50 million. Predict whether interest coverage stays at or above 2.0 times after the next reset.</p>
<form><p><label>Reference rate (%) <select><option>2</option><option>3</option><option selected>4</option><option>4.1</option><option>5</option><option>6</option></select></label></p>
<p><label>Debt resetting (%) <select><option>0</option><option>25</option><option>50</option><option>75</option><option selected>100</option></select></label></p>
<p><label>Annual EBIT (HK$ million) <select><option>5.4</option><option selected>6</option><option>7</option><option>7.2</option></select></label></p><button type="reset">Reset scenario</button></form>
<div aria-live="polite" class="scenario-result"></div>
<details><summary>Check the calculation</summary><p class="scenario-math"></p></details>
<p><strong>Make the call.</strong> Which action would you recommend? Give a figure and the assumption that matters most.</p>
<details><summary>Compare your recommendation</summary><p class="scenario-call"></p></details>
<noscript>Enable JavaScript to change scenarios. The worked example below explains the decision.</noscript>
</section>
<script>
(() => {
  const lab = document.getElementById('policy-transmission-lab');
  const form = lab.querySelector('form');
  const format = n => n.toLocaleString('en-US', {minimumFractionDigits: 2, maximumFractionDigits: 2});
  const money = n => 'HK$' + format(n);
  const usd = n => 'US$' + format(n);
  function calculate(inputs) {
    const [ref,share,ebit]=inputs;
const interest=50*((ref+2)*share/100+5*(1-share/100))/100;
const cover=ebit/interest,room=ebit-2*interest;
return {rows:[['Annual interest',money(interest*1e6)],['Coverage',cover.toFixed(3)+'×'],['EBIT above covenant minimum',money(room*1e6)]],bars:[['Coverage',+cover.toFixed(3)],['Covenant minimum',2]],math:'The resetting portion pays the reference rate plus 2 percentage points. The balance pays 5%. Coverage = annual EBIT ÷ annual interest.',call:Math.abs(room)<1e-9?'Exactly at the minimum. Any decline in EBIT would trigger a breach under these terms.':room<0?'Contact the lender before the test. The borrower needs '+money(-room*1e6)+' more annual EBIT to reach the minimum.':'The borrower passes with '+money(room*1e6)+' of EBIT headroom. Confirm the fixing and test dates.'};
  }
  function refresh() {
    const inputs = Array.from(form.querySelectorAll('select'), field => Number.isFinite(Number(field.value)) ? Number(field.value) : field.value);
    const result = calculate(inputs);
    const table = document.createElement('table');
    table.setAttribute('aria-label', 'Scenario results');
    for (const [label, value] of result.rows) {
      const row = table.insertRow();
      const heading = document.createElement('th');
      heading.scope = 'row';
      heading.textContent = label;
      row.append(heading);
      row.insertCell().textContent = value;
    }
    const output = lab.querySelector('.scenario-result');
    output.replaceChildren(table);
    if (result.bars) {
      const maximum = Math.max(...result.bars.map(item => item[1]));
      for (const [label, value] of result.bars) {
        const line = document.createElement('p');
        const bar = document.createElement('meter');
        bar.max = maximum;
        bar.value = value;
        bar.setAttribute('aria-label', label);
        line.append(label + ' ', bar, ' ' + value);
        output.append(line);
      }
    }
    lab.querySelector('.scenario-math').textContent = result.math;
    lab.querySelector('.scenario-call').textContent = result.call;
  }
  form.addEventListener('change', refresh);
  form.addEventListener('reset', () => requestAnimationFrame(refresh));
  refresh();
})();
</script>
<section aria-label="Practice brief"><h2>When should the relationship manager reopen the covenant discussion?</h2><details><summary>Compare your recommendation</summary><p>At HK$6 million of annual EBIT, two-times coverage allows HK$3 million of annual interest. On HK$50 million of debt that puts the all-in rate ceiling at 6%, or a 4% reference rate plus the 2-point spread. At the ceiling there is no headroom. If the next fixing takes the reference rate above 4%, open the covenant discussion before the test date. Recalculate if EBIT changes or only part of the loan resets.</p></details></section>
```

**Teaching source.** Week 9 develops monetary and fiscal transmission using IS–LM and IS–MP. Loan terms, the coverage threshold, and EBIT scenarios are illustrative.
